rationale.text: The correction follows the stated rule rather than the proposed alternative. An original United States Social Security card or Canadian social insurance card qualifies as secondary identity evidence.

lines.text: An extra paper is not automatically qualifying evidence.

narration.text: Secondary evidence is a defined list rather than a label for any extra paper. The original Social Security or Canadian social insurance card is one category, and a government-issued certified marriage certificate or license is another. The source also gives a bounded secondary use for certain expired jurisdiction-issued credentials. Keep those qualifications with the document name. A remembered number is not the same evidence as the original card, and a private celebration invitation is not the certified government marriage record described by the source.

lines.text: Issuer, fields and status can change the category.
Current government-employee photo identification, a current jurisdiction-issued credential without a color photograph and a certified
court order or judgment occupy different secondary categories.

narration.text: Current government-employee photo identification, a current jurisdiction-issued credential without a color photograph and a certified court order or judgment occupy different secondary categories. The court record needs the applicant’s full legal name and birth date. A previously accepted USCIS primary document may have a limited secondary allowance after expiration, while a certified birth certificate from outside the listed domestic and Canadian areas has its own secondary placement. Notice how issuer, fields, expiration and jurisdiction can change the classification without making every category identical.

lines.text: Related paperwork is not always the listed document.
Several secondary categories depend on the applicant’s individual connection to the record.

narration.text: Several secondary categories depend on the applicant’s individual connection to the record. A release or discharge certification is the named military record; the health-program or insurance card shows the person’s name and individual number. The firearm-permit category requires the specified official issuer, current status and color photo. A current federal pilot license is another named category. Do not substitute a generally related receipt, workplace reference or travel record. The source identifies particular documents whose required details connect them to the applicant.

lines.text: Different records establish their connection in different ways.
School-related secondary evidence also has distinct conditions.

narration.text: School-related secondary evidence also has distinct conditions. Certified records or transcripts carry the applicant’s full name, preferably with birth date. The approved traffic-education completion certificate includes name and birth date, while the current school photo ID includes the student’s name and number. A child’s certified birth record can support the parent applicant when it lists that parent with name and birth date in the described way. These examples are not interchangeable simply because they involve education or family. Read the particular identifying connection in each category.

lines.text: An identity document still needs the required address for residence use.
Residence evidence answers a location question rather than only an identity question.

narration.text: Residence evidence answers a location question rather than only an identity question. The original applicant proves the Montana residence address and supplies a separate mailing address when mail cannot be received there. The evidence shows the applicant’s name and residence address matching the application. The source lists identity, tax, voter, property-tax and insurance records with their relevant conditions. An accepted document type without the needed address does not complete this purpose. Keep the applicant, the physical residence and the matching evidence connected throughout the review.

lines.text: Alternative evidence routes still have their own conditions.

narration.text: Other residence routes have specific supporting details. School records retain an attendance window and the required name and address. A listed family member’s shared-residence confirmation comes with that person’s permitted address document. Rental evidence is original and signed as described; mortgage or home-equity papers show the applicant’s location, including the stated rural-address allowance. Common payroll, banking, utility and mail records also have a recent-issuance condition. These are alternative evidence routes, but each route keeps its own fields, timing and supporting-record requirements.

lines.text: A number, a card and a location answer different questions.

narration.text: Check the original-card distinction in the secondary list. Does merely remembering a Social Security number supply the original card category? No; the source names the actual original card. Then shift to residence: does a convenient mailing address replace proof of where the applicant lives? No; the purposes are separate. For a person experiencing homelessness, the source provides a descriptive location, separate mailing address and agency-letterhead verification route. That route supplies a way to document the situation rather than treating the lack of a conventional home as permission to omit the address process.

lines.text: Read the whole evidence route before accepting its label.

narration.text: Read the secondary and residence lists with the same disciplined method. Identify the purpose of the step, find the source’s accepted document category and retain its name, address, photo, certification or timing conditions. For shared residence or homelessness, keep the supporting statement and verification requirements visible. This approach helps avoid two common shortcuts: treating every school paper as the same identity evidence, or treating any mailed item as proof of physical residence. A school record’s fields and an address record’s timing both matter; the general document name does not remove those conditions.

why_how.text: The source keeps document integrity and required official checking within each step. Submitting a document title alone does not meet every condition.
The source combines identity fields with the specified citizenship or lawful-presence basis. It is more than a request for any card bearing a name.
The source requires the full number with the applicant’s name and describes agency checking. A partial or unrelated identifier does not match that evidence rule.
The source requires a pair of acceptable records and attaches currency conditions to them. The address is the applicant’s current physical location.
The source allows same-type documents while retaining their other acceptance conditions. Same type does not mean missing name or address becomes acceptable.
The source requires a documented chain linking the names. Evidence of only the latest name does not necessarily establish every intervening legal change.

scenario.text: A learner faces this decision: How must documents supplied for the REAL ID steps be presented?

reasoning.text: The proposed response is “Altered to match the requested result.”. That alternative does not preserve the stated rule. REAL ID applicants must provide unaltered required documents for each required step, with agency certification or MVD verification where required.

result.text: Choose “Unaltered, with certification or verification where required.”. Keep the setting and every stated condition attached to that response.

claim.text: Common mistake: “Altered to match the requested result.”.

correction.text: REAL ID applicants must provide unaltered required documents for each required step, with agency certification or MVD verification where required.

memory_support.text: Remember “REAL ID documentation”. Connect the person or setting to the required action, then check the full statement for limits or exceptions.

prompt.text: Consider the earlier decision. Is “Altered to match the requested result.” a sound response? Give the correction and explain the condition that decides it.

answer.text: REAL ID applicants must provide unaltered required documents for each required step, with agency certification or MVD verification where required.

rationale.text: The correction follows the stated rule rather than the proposed alternative. REAL ID applicants must provide unaltered required documents for each required step, with agency certification or MVD verification where required.

lines.text: Each step establishes a particular part of the application.

narration.text: REAL ID is presented as a sequence of evidence steps, with unaltered documents and required certification or verification. Start by identifying what each step establishes rather than assuming one card completes the whole process. The identity step includes current legal name, birth date and citizenship or other lawful federal authorization. The Social Security and residence steps ask for their own evidence. Keeping these purposes separate helps the learner understand why an otherwise familiar document may not answer the particular question being checked at that point in the application.

lines.text: The evidence must identify this applicant for the stated check.
The REAL ID Social Security evidence shows the applicant’s name and full issued number for
checking with the Social Security Administration.

narration.text: The REAL ID Social Security evidence shows the applicant’s name and full issued number for checking with the Social Security Administration. That is more specific than supplying any partial identifier or a number associated with a different person. Compare it with the identity step, which establishes current legal name, birth date and the stated citizenship or lawful-presence basis. Both concern the same applicant, but they do not ask the same evidence question. Preserve the required identifying link instead of treating an abbreviated or unrelated number as automatically sufficient.

title.text: Two Records With The Required Address

lines.text: Same type does not remove the other acceptance conditions.
The REAL ID residence step uses two acceptable documents with the applicant’s name and current
physical address, subject to the source’s currency conditions.

narration.text: The REAL ID residence step uses two acceptable documents with the applicant’s name and current physical address, subject to the source’s currency conditions. The two may be of the same type. That allowance concerns document type, not permission to omit the name, address or status requirements. Imagine two records from the same category: the category match is allowed, but each still has to meet the conditions for acceptable residence evidence. A convenient mailing destination alone should not be substituted for the current physical-address question this step asks.

lines.text: Document the changes rather than altering the evidence.

narration.text: A legal name difference requires a documented connection between the current name and the earlier evidence. The source asks for every legal change back to the original documented name, rather than only an explanation of the latest nickname. Think of a chain with several links: showing the last link does not necessarily explain how the current record connects to the first. Do not repair the mismatch by hand-altering required documents. Keep the documentary chain and the integrity requirement together so the current identity can be related to the records used in the application.

lines.text: A name change needs evidence, not a hand-edited record.

narration.text: Check the integrity rule across the REAL ID steps. Can an applicant hand-edit a required document to make the name match? No; the source requires unaltered documents with the required official checking. If the legal name changed, use the documented chain instead. Then identify what remains in the other steps: evidence of the full issued Social Security number and the required pair of residence records. Completing one step does not authorize skipping the others. Explain how the documents connect to the same applicant while serving different verification purposes.

lines.text: Separate purposes while connecting the same applicant.

narration.text: Use the REAL ID sequence as a final exercise in reading conditions. Establish the current identity and lawful-presence basis, connect the issued Social Security number to the applicant, supply the required physical-address evidence and document any legal name changes. Keep documents unaltered and retain the stated official certification or verification. A missing link, altered record or incomplete address combination can leave a separate step unanswered. The learning outcome is a faithful understanding of the steps and their relationships, without promising that a partial stack of papers completes the entire application.
